title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #10

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which are the three states of matter? (1 mark)
   A. Solid, liquid and gas
   B. Hot, warm and cold
   C. Big, medium and small
   D. Hard, soft and rough

2. Which state of matter has no fixed shape and no fixed volume? (1 mark)
   A. Solid
   B. Powder
   C. Liquid
   D. Gas

3. Which is an example of reducing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Throwing a bottle in a river
   B. Burning plastic
   C. Leaving litter at a picnic
   D. Carrying a cloth shopping bag

4. In a seedling, what is the correct order of growth? (1 mark)
   A. Seed, root, shoot with leaves
   B. Shoot, seed, root
   C. Root, flower, seed
   D. Leaves, seed, root

5. There are 750 ml of milk in a jug. 300 ml is poured out. How much is left? (1 mark)
   A. 550 ml
   B. 350 ml
   C. 450 ml
   D. 1050 ml

6. Which of these statements about matter is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Gases have no mass
   B. Only liquids have mass
   C. Only solids have mass
   D. Solids, liquids and gases all have mass

7. What is vomiting? (1 mark)
   A. Passing loose faeces
   B. Food coming out through the mouth
   C. Chewing food
   D. Feeling hungry

8. What do solar panels change sunlight into? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Food
   C. Electricity
   D. Sound

9. Which of these can be a cheap way of lighting a house in a rural area? (1 mark)
   A. Hundreds of candles
   B. Solar lamp
   C. Many electric heaters
   D. A big generator

10. What is digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Breaking down food into tiny parts the body can use
   B. Making food hot
   C. Storing food in the stomach for years
   D. Throwing away food

11. Pulling a rope in tug of war uses (1 mark)
   A. Only gravity
   B. Only light
   C. Only heat
   D. A pull force

12. Which of these is transparent? (1 mark)
   A. Thick cardboard
   B. Metal
   C. Clear glass
   D. Wood

13. What does recycle mean? (1 mark)
   A. Throw waste away
   B. Make waste into new things
   C. Bury waste
   D. Burn waste

14. Which part of the digestive system is the widest tube near the end? (1 mark)
   A. Anus
   B. Small intestine
   C. Large intestine
   D. Gullet

15. Which force makes it hard to push a heavy box along a rough floor? (1 mark)
   A. Light
   B. Colour
   C. Friction
   D. Sound

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. State three things that plants give to people. (3 marks)

17. A shopkeeper has 2 kg of sugar and 750 g of salt. Find the total mass in grams. (3 marks)

18. Explain the difference between reusing and recycling. (3 marks)

19. Describe how you would show that air takes up space using a cup, tissue paper and a basin of water. (4 marks)

20. State two functions of roots. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Solid, liquid and gas
   Matter exists as solids, liquids and gases.

2. D — Gas
   Gases spread out to fill all the space.

3. D — Carrying a cloth shopping bag
   A reusable bag means fewer plastic bags are thrown away.

4. A — Seed, root, shoot with leaves
   The seed starts, a root comes out, then a shoot with leaves.

5. C — 450 ml
   750 - 300 = 450 ml.

6. D — Solids, liquids and gases all have mass
   All matter has mass, whatever its state.

7. B — Food coming out through the mouth
   Vomiting is throwing up food through the mouth.

8. C — Electricity
   Solar panels make electricity from sunlight.

9. B — Solar lamp
   Solar lamps use free energy from the sun.

10. A — Breaking down food into tiny parts the body can use
   Digestion breaks food into tiny parts that can pass into the blood.

11. D — A pull force
   Pulling is a force.

12. C — Clear glass
   Clear glass lets light through.

13. B — Make waste into new things
   Recycling makes new things from old materials.

14. C — Large intestine
   The large intestine is wider than the small intestine.

15. C — Friction
   Rough floor gives large friction.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Food, shade, wood, medicine, clean air (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2750 g.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 2 kg = 2000 g, 1 mark for adding 750 g and 1 mark for the answer.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Reusing means using an item again in the same or a new way without changing it, for example a bottle for water. Recycling means turning waste into a new product, for example melting old plastic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reuse, 1 mark for recycle, 1 mark for one example.

19. (4 marks)
   Answer: Push dry tissue into the bottom of the cup. Turn the cup upside down and push it straight down into water. Lift it out. The tissue is dry because air took up the space in the cup and kept the water out.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for pushing into water, 1 mark for dry tissue, 1 mark for conclusion.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: They hold the plant in the soil and take in water and mineral salts. Some store food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct function.
